clauses.label: Section 1.
clauses.text:
Section 1. Establishm ent, (a) There is established the Chemical Warfare  
Review Commission. The Commission shall be composed of no more than nine  
members appointed or designated by the President. The membership shall be  
bipartisan.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) The President shall designate a Chairman from among the members of the  
Commission.

clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text:
Sec. 2. Functions, (a) The Commission shall review the overall adequacy of the  
chemical warfare posture of the United States with particular emphasis on the  
question of whether the United* States should produce binary chemical muni­
tions. In conducting its review, the Commission shall take account of the  
considerations specified in Section 1511 of Public Law 98-525.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) The Commission shall make sequential reports to the President on its  
findings and recommendations, by February 15, 1985, as to the need to  
maintain a chemical retaliatory stockpile; by March 1,1985, as to the adequa­
cy of the current stockpile if one has been determined to be needed; and by  
March 15, 1985, as to whether the United States should produce binary  
chemical munitions or undertake other actions.

clauses.label: Sec. 3.
clauses.text:
Sec. 3. Adm inistration, (a) The heads of Executive agencies shall, to the extent  
permitted by law, provide the Commission such information as it may require  
for purposes of carrying out its functions.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) Members of the Commission shall serve without any additional compensa­
tion for their work on the Commission. However, members appointed from  
among private citizens may be allowed travel expenses, including per diem in  
lieu of subsistence, as authorized by law for persons serving intermittently in  
the government service (5 U.S.C. 5701-5707), to the extent funds are available  
therefor.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) The Secretary of Defense shall provide the Commission with such adminis­
trative services, facilities, staff and other support services as may be neces­
sary. Any expenses of the Commission shall be paid from such funds as may  
be available to the Secretary of Defense.

own_original_text:
Executive Order 12502 of January 28, 1985
Chemical Warfare Review Commission
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution of the laws of  
the United States of America, and in order to establish, in accordance with the  
provisions of Section 1511 of the Department of Defense Authorization Act,  
1985 (Public Law 98-525), and of the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as  
amended (5 U.S.C. App. I), a Chemical Warfare Review Commission, it is  
hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. Establishm ent, (a) There is established the Chemical Warfare  
Review Commission. The Commission shall be composed of no more than nine  
members appointed or designated by the President. The membership shall be  
bipartisan.
(b) The President shall designate a Chairman from among the members of the  
Commission.
Sec. 2. Functions, (a) The Commission shall review the overall adequacy of the  
chemical warfare posture of the United States with particular emphasis on the  
question of whether the United* States should produce binary chemical muni­
tions. In conducting its review, the Commission shall take account of the  
considerations specified in Section 1511 of Public Law 98-525.
(b) The Commission shall make sequential reports to the President on its  
findings and recommendations, by February 15, 1985, as to the need to  
maintain a chemical retaliatory stockpile; by March 1,1985, as to the adequa­
cy of the current stockpile if one has been determined to be needed; and by  
March 15, 1985, as to whether the United States should produce binary  
chemical munitions or undertake other actions.
Sec. 3. Adm inistration, (a) The heads of Executive agencies shall, to the extent  
permitted by law, provide the Commission such information as it may require  
for purposes of carrying out its functions.
(b) Members of the Commission shall serve without any additional compensa­
tion for their work on the Commission. However, members appointed from  
among private citizens may be allowed travel expenses, including per diem in  
lieu of subsistence, as authorized by law for persons serving intermittently in  
the government service (5 U.S.C. 5701-5707), to the extent funds are available  
therefor.
(c) The Secretary of Defense shall provide the Commission with such adminis­
trative services, facilities, staff and other support services as may be neces­
sary. Any expenses of the Commission shall be paid from such funds as may  
be available to the Secretary of Defense.

versions.research_rationale: EO 12502 (Jan. 28, 1985; 50 FR 4195) established the Chemical Warfare Review Commission under FACA and Pub. L. 98-525 sec. 1511; its nine operative subsections all concern the Commission. Section 4(b) ends it '30 days after submission of its report, or on September 30,1985, whichever date is earlier'; sequential reports were due by February 15, March 1 and March 15, 1985 (sec. 2(b)). No amendment exists. The end is therefore no later than September 30, 1985 and earlier if the report was submitted before August 31, 1985, which no held source settles. EO 12534 sec. 3(a), effective September 30, 1985, lists it among terminated committees. The first-end date is left open. The draft's FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT is resolved by reading EO 12534 sec. 3, which revokes each listed order as a whole; the 'partial' reading came only from the OFR catalog's acting-order phrasing 'Revokes advisory committees established by'. No human certification is asserted.

savings_residuals.reason: Neither EO 12502 nor the revoking EO 12534 contains a savings clause, and EO 12534 sec. 3 states that the committees it lists had already terminated. Members served without additional compensation, and the Defense support and FACA delegation in secs. 3(c) and 4(a) applied only to the Commission; the statutory review mandate of Pub. L. 98-525 sec. 1511 was discharged through the Commission's reports and is not an effect of this order. No rights, entitlements, property, delegations or functions outside the body itself were created, so nothing survives its termination; reimbursements and support given while it existed are completed transactions, not continuing effects. Bounded search: the full original order, every amending and continuance order named in this claim, and EO 12534.

unresolved_material_gaps: ending_or_current_basis: the first end of every clause (and so whole_order_end) is not established. Sec. 4(b) ends the Commission 30 days after submission of its report, or on September 30, 1985, whichever is earlier; the reports were due in February-March 1985. No held source records the date the report was actually submitted, and a reporting deadline is not evidence of that date. EO 12534 sec. 3 (effective 1985-09-30) is a cleanup revocation of a body it describes as already terminated, so it cannot be used as the first end. Needed: an official record of the report's transmittal date (for example the Weekly Compilation of Presidential Documents or the report itself), queued through FETCH_QUEUE.jsonl.
ending_or_current_basis: Pub. L. 98-525 sec. 1511 (98 Stat.) is not held; read it for any statutory term of the Commission.
claim.research_rationale: EO 12502 (Jan. 28, 1985; 50 FR 4195) established the Chemical Warfare Review Commission under FACA and Pub. L. 98-525 sec. 1511; its nine operative subsections all concern the Commission. Section 4(b) ends it '30 days after submission of its report, or on September 30,1985, whichever date is earlier'; sequential reports were due by February 15, March 1 and March 15, 1985 (sec. 2(b)). No amendment exists. The end is therefore no later than September 30, 1985 and earlier if the report was submitted before August 31, 1985, which no held source settles. EO 12534 sec. 3(a), effective September 30, 1985, lists it among terminated committees. The first-end date is left open. The draft's FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT is resolved by reading EO 12534 sec. 3, which revokes each listed order as a whole; the 'partial' reading came only from the OFR catalog's acting-order phrasing 'Revokes advisory committees established by'. No human certification is asserted.
